unit.why: A single tale told by R. Shalom Rokeach of Belz at the third Sabbath meal: a thoroughly wicked man risks death to keep the mitzvah of hand-washing and so gains the World to Come.

stories.start_quote: כ) מעשה נטילת ידים מאדון עוזינו
stories.summary_en: At the third Sabbath meal in 5614 the Belzer rebbe tells of a wicked man who sinned in every way except hand-washing before meals; travelling on Hol ha-Moed Pesach, he went to a well among robbers rather than eat unwashed, was killed, and received a place in the upper Garden of Eden, and the rebbe draws the lesson for keeping all the commandments.

quotes: והגאון הצדיק ספר זאת המעשה בשעת שלש סעודות
ששמעו נא מורי ורבותי מעשה שהי׳ כך
tags.why: The rebbe narrates the tale at a set occasion.
The frame is the third Sabbath meal.
The rebbe tells the story with fervor.
The stated aim is to arouse fear of Heaven.

quotes: פעם אחת הוצרך בחול המועד פסח
tags.why: The inner tale takes place on Hol ha-Moed Pesach.

quotes: מצוה אחת דרבנן והוא נטילת ידים לסעודה
tags.why: The rabbinic commandment of hand-washing, and matzah versus hametz, are central to the plot.

quotes: ולא אבה לאכול או לטעום כל לחם בלי נטילת ידים
tags.why: Though starving, he refuses to eat without washing.

quotes: הלא ידעתי כי שמה שודדים גזלנים ורוצחי נפש
tags.why: He fears the robbers at the well.
The man is killed by the robbers.
The heavenly uproar and the judgment in Gan Eden are depicted.

quotes: אם על מצוה אחת דרבנן נחל העוה״ב
tags.why: Reward in the World to Come is the point of the tale.

quotes: על אחת כמה וכמה אם ישמור האדם
tags.why: The rebbe closes with a homiletic lesson.

missing_concepts: reward for a single commandment (sakhar mitzvah)
hand-washing before meals (netilat yadayim) as a theme
